title: Grand Canyon
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Grand Canyon”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. The Grand Canyon is 277 miles (446 km) long, up to 18 miles (29 km) wide and attains a depth of over a mile (6,093 feet or 1,857 meters).

The canyon and adjacent rim are contained within Grand Canyon National Park, the Kaibab National Forest, Grand Canyon–Parashant National Monument, the Hualapai Indian Reservation, the Havasupai Indian Reservation and the Navajo Nation. President Theodore Roosevelt was a major proponent of the preservation of the Grand Canyon area and visited it on numerous occasions to hunt and enjoy the scenery.

Nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history have been exposed as the Colorado River and its tributaries cut their channels through layer after layer of rock while the Colorado Plateau was uplifted. While some aspects about the history of incision of the canyon are debated by geologists, several recent studies support the hypothesis that the Colorado River established its course through the area about 5 to 6 million years ago. Since that time, the Colorado River has driven the down-cutting of the tributaries and retreat of the cliffs, simultaneously deepening and widening the canyon.

For thousands of years, the area has been continuously inhabited by Native Americans, who built settlements within the canyon and its many caves. The Pueblo people considered the Grand Canyon a holy site, and made pilgrimages to it. The first European known to have viewed the Grand Canyon was García López de Cárdenas from Spain, who arrived in 1540.

sentence.text: Nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history have been exposed as the Colorado River and its tributaries cut their channels through layer after layer of rock while the Colorado Plateau was uplifted.
sentence.translation: 科罗拉多河及其支流切穿一层又一层岩石，开辟河道，同时科罗拉多高原不断抬升，使地球近二十亿年的地质历史显露出来。
sentence.analysis: 主句是 Nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history have been exposed，其中 have been exposed 是现在完成时的被动语态，强调地质历史已经通过岩层显露出来。as 引导状语从句，交代这一结果发生的过程和背景，可理解为“随着……”。该从句的主语是 the Colorado River and its tributaries，谓语是 cut，their channels 是宾语，through layer after layer of rock 表示切穿的路径。while 引导更内层的时间状语从句，说明河流下切期间高原也在抬升；was uplifted 是一般过去时的被动语态。

questions.prompt: 文中“近二十亿年”和“五至六百万年”这两组时间分别指什么？
options: 现今国家公园建立和扩建的时间
显露出的地质历史跨度，以及部分研究认为科罗拉多河在此确立河道的大致时间
欧洲人到达该地区与当地人开始定居的时间
大峡谷的宽度变化与深度变化所用的时间
questions.explanation: 第三段的 nearly two billion years 修饰 Earth's geological history，指被岩层揭示的历史跨度；5 to 6 million years ago 则用于说明关于河道形成时间的研究假说。两者不能都当作峡谷本身的年龄。

questions.prompt: 最后一段如何帮助读者理解 1540 年这件事？
options: 它是文中首位已知看见大峡谷的欧洲人到来的年份，而当地原住民在此前已生活数千年
它是普韦布洛人首次将大峡谷视为圣地的确切年份
它说明大峡谷在欧洲人到来之前没有任何居民
它标志着人类第一次在大峡谷地区定居
questions.explanation: 最后一段先说原住民已在此连续居住数千年，随后才说明 García López de Cárdenas 是已知首位看到大峡谷的欧洲人，抵达时间为 1540 年。“首位欧洲人”不等于“首位人类”。
